Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightline.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Upfront commitment / how to allocate across FYs for accounting

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the platform checks a lot of boxes. We are comfortable moving forward with the 36-month committed capacity, but before I sign the SOW I need clarity on two finance items our CFO raised:

1) Our controller needs the invoice schedule broken down by Redwood's suggested allocation for our FYs so we can map to our budget. We close our fiscal year on 2027-06-30.
2) How Redwood expects to handle revenue recognition for a multi-year upfront payment — specifically whether you can provide an invoice split that matches service delivery for ASC 606 treatment.

Can you propose a simple split and note any revenue recognition constraints that would affect our internal accounting? Also include any discount steps tied to ramping usage in Year 2/3 so we can bake this into our forecasting.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — hoping to route the SOW to Legal and Procurement by end of next week.

Best,
Daniel Hart
CFO, Brightline Health

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Upfront commitment / how to allocate across FYs for accounting

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the clear ask. Quick summary up front: Redwood can accept a single upfront payment and issue invoices split across fiscal years for your controller to recognize revenue in line with service delivery. We typically recommend a pragmatic allocation rather than equal annual slices when customers have a mid‑FY close like yours.

Proposed high-level invoice allocation (attached workbook with line items):
- Invoice 1 (paid at signing): 50% of committed value — Redwood will invoice this as "Year 1 allocation".
- Invoice 2 (12 months after signing): 30% — allocated across remaining service months in FY1/FY2 depending on sign date.
- Invoice 3 (24 months after signing): 20% — allocated to the final 12 months.

Rationale: this frontloads cash for capacity provisioning but still allows you to map revenue to delivery periods. If you prefer smoother budget impact we can move to a 40/35/25 split or a per‑fiscal‑year slice (e.g., 60% FY27, 40% FY28) — I included both permutations in the attached Invoice_Allocation_Proposal.xlsx.

Accounting note from Karthik (cc'd): if Brightline pays the full upfront amount, Redwood will record deferred revenue and recognize revenue over the pattern of service. We can provide a simple allocation table and a one‑page rev‑rec memo (ASC 606) for your controller to sign off. Important caveat: discounts tied to future usage ramps must be documented in the contract language so they aren't treated as variable consideration that would change recognized revenue amounts retroactively.

Next steps I propose:
- Marissa to create an updated SOW numbering the invoices and inserting language that the upfront payment will be invoiced in three installments as listed.
- Karthik will draft the rev‑rec memo and a short accounting FAQ.
- Daniel to confirm the preferred split (50/30/20 or alternate).

I attached the workbook with the sample allocations and sample contract language snippets. Let us know which option you prefer and we will produce an updated SOW + invoice schedule.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20‑minute call if that helps.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(650) 555-0123

Daniel —

Following up from Stephanie: we can update the SOW to enumerate three invoices and include explicit contract language about the discount schedule and non‑recourse on future usage. Two pragmatic notes from Ops:

• If Brightline wants a fiscal‑year boundary allocation (so the entire FY27 cost is contained in FY27), we can do a 60% invoice at signing and 40% in Year 2. That simplifies your controller's mapping but shifts more cash to Year 1.

• Alternatively we can draft an amortization appendix for your controller showing how Redwood will defer revenue and recognize it monthly over the term; that appendix speeds approvals for customers who want to see the rev‑rec math.

I added an extra tab in the allocation workbook with the three variants and a column that shows the monthly recognized revenue under Redwood's standard pattern.

If you'd like, I'm happy to lock in the 50/30/20 by the end of the day and circulate an SOW with numbered invoice lines and payment dates tied to signature + 12/24 months.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Daniel —

Quick technical note from our accounting team to help your controller:

1) If Brightline prepays the full committed amount, Redwood will classify payment as deferred revenue on our balance sheet and will recognize revenue ratably over the period of the contract (monthly). We can provide the monthly recognition schedule so your controller can mirror it.

2) Discounts tied to guaranteed usage (e.g., 15% discount in Year 2 if you hit X tokens) are treated as variable consideration under ASC 606. To avoid impacts to prior period recognition, we recommend documenting an objective, measurable ramp metric in the SOW and capping the discount exposure. Alternatively, treat the discount as a credit applied to future invoices (preferred).

3) For audit purposes, we'll include a one‑page rev‑rec memo and the recognition table as an appendix to the SOW. That memo will state: payment received in full; revenue recognized monthly; any contingent discounts recognized when earned and constrained per ASC 606.

If Brightline's controller needs us to sign a short attestation that the allocation table represents Redwood's expected recognition pattern, we can provide that.

Happy to hop on a quick call with your accounting team — available 1–3pm PT today.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Finance Ops
Redwood Inference
